description:
FILED + FIXED s470br (Opus, 2026-09-05), from Fable's review of #1115.

`use open` is LEXICAL in perl and PCL's first implementation (#1115) made it a
runtime GLOBAL.  Measured on an 11-octet file (8 characters decoded), with a
module whose own top carries `use open qw(:utf8)`:

    main-plain: 11  module-utf8: 8 / block-utf8: 8 / after-block-plain: 11   perl
    main-plain:  8  module-utf8: 8 / block-utf8: 8 / after-block-plain:  8   PCL

So the MODULE's pragma changed the calling program's plain `open`, and a
block-scoped one leaked to the rest of the file.  Before #1115 this was masked
(everything decoded anyway); once bytes are the default it is a silent WRONG â
any CPAN module carrying `use open` flips its caller's I/O.

FIX (the shape Fable designed, with one measured deviation):
  * `Pl::Parser::_use_open_layers` reads the pragma's LIST statically (the list
    is a compile-time fact; all 7 shapes in perl's t/, perl-tests/, lib/ and the
    CPAN board are qw()/quoted/fat-comma -- surveyed, 71 statements, no computed
    element; a non-literal one ANNOUNCES rather than guessing).
  * `open_regions_of` turns them into SOURCE-LOCATION spans (pragma statement ->
    end of its enclosing BLOCK, or end of document at file level), and
    `open_layers_at` answers a site: innermost wins, and an inner pragma
    overrides only the directions it names, as ${^OPEN} does.
  * The spans are published by a PARSER2 PRE-PASS through
    `fallback_parser->lex_home->{_open_regions}`.  A scope-stack pragma CANNOT
    work and that was measured: a named sub's BODY is lowered before the
    in-stream include statement is reached (task #703's finding), so the
    module's own `use open` had no effect on its own sub.
  * `ExprToCL::_wrap_default_layers` emits `(p-default-layers (IN OUT) CALL)` at
    `p-open` and `p-backtick` -- perldoc open's own list is "open() and
    readpipe(), as well as qx// and ``", so NOT sysopen/opendir/pipe.
  * `p-use-open` now does ONLY the `:std` half (perl applies that once, at the
    pragma) and is emitted only for a list containing `:std`.

THE DEVIATION, and it is perl's own answer: **`no open` is a NO-OP**.  perl's
open.pm defines `import` and NO `unimport` (5.40.3), so
`use open qw(:utf8); no open; open â¦` still decodes (probed: 8, not 11) and
`no open ':utf8'` is a FATAL "Attempt to call undefined unimport method".  The
first version truncated the region at a `no open`; the probe killed it.

BARS: 8/8 probe rows identical to perl (module, block, nested IN=>':raw',
`no open`, IN/OUT split, `:std`); corpus-diff vs 027ba9c 4 of 111 with every
diff explained; emission-ab over the 127-file union population 67 DIFF /
RCDIFF 0 / 0 unexplained; four guard rows in Pl/t/io-layers-01.t, all failing
on a base extraction.
subject: `use open` is LEXICAL in perl and #1115 made it a runtime GLOBAL â a module's own pragma changed its CALLER's I/O and a block-scoped one leaked; the layers now ride each open SITE
